payload.name: ExtractPerMemberAttributesFromEnumerations
payload.description: When a message assigns separate attributes to multiple distinct members of a group using names, ordinals, or other identifiers, extract one memory candidate per member during construction.
content: During candidate extraction, if a user enumerates distinct members of a group and gives each a different quality (e.g., 'oldest is...', 'second is...', 'youngest is...'), create a separate candidate for each member, preserving the member identifier in the memory text.
Do not merge the enumeration into one generic memory such as 'all members have personalities' and do not skip it because the group is informal or unnamed.
For each candidate, store the specific attribute as a stable profile fact about that member and include enough context (e.g., 'oldest pet', 'second child') to distinguish it from other members.

candidates.solves: A construction pass can silently drop an explicit per-member enumeration ('oldest is relaxed, second is playful') by treating it as one anecdote. This rule forces one memory candidate per enumerated member so each attribute is preserved. Applies whenever a message labels distinct entities and assigns each its own attribute; not when the group is described only collectively.

payload.name: Persist explicit counts for tracked group additions
payload.description: When a conversation introduces a new member of a countable group already tracked in memory, add or update an explicit total-count memory at decision time.
content: When a message or extraction candidate introduces a new member of a group already tracked as separate member memories, also create or update an aggregate count/state memory (ADD or UPDATE) at decision time; do not only enrich an existing event memory.
Record the current total and the as-of date from the message timestamp, keeping it concise, e.g., 'X has N [group members] as of [date]', using memory kind state.

candidates.solves: When a user reveals a new addition to a countable group already tracked via separate member memories, the agent often records only the new event and never persists an explicit total, so later count questions fail. This applies during construction decisions whenever a new member joins a previously tracked group: add or update an aggregate count/state memory. Do not apply when no prior members exist or the total is not clearly evidenced.

payload.name: Store explicit counts for sets of owned entities
payload.description: When construction extracts a new member of an existing set of entities owned by a person (e.g., pets, children, vehicles), store the updated total count explicitly in the profile or state memory.
content: If a message introduces a new instance of a category the person already has (e.g., another pet, child, car), after recording the new instance also update or create a memory stating the total number of that category, e.g., 'Person has N X.'
When updating an existing memory that lists members of a set, ensure the explicit count is included in the updated content and not left implicit.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction stored individual dog adoptions but never recorded the running total, so a later count query could only infer the number from listed names. The rule generalizes the mechanism of maintaining explicit set-size in memory whenever a new member is added. It applies to any future conversation where a person's countable possessions or family members grow over multiple sessions, so that count-based questions are answerable without re-inferring from names.

candidate_resolutions.reason: No existing Skill covers per-member attribute extraction from enumerations.
Merged with candidate 89e54cb7eacb because both repair the same mechanism of persisting explicit counts for tracked groups.
Creates one merged Skill for explicit count persistence.
